who.value: buyer checking out a bulky-delivery item

job.value: review address, deal method and payment, then place the order

arrivedFrom.value: Buy on the listing or chat

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: 'Order request' with the sofa bed, 'Address', 'Deal method', 'Payment' and 'Promo code' rows reads plainly as checkout.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: 'Place order' is pinned at the bottom but greyed out until 'Deal method' is added, and on the first screen the teal 'Add'/'Edit' links compete with nothing stronger.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Edit' and 'Add' on each section and 'Place order' all predict their result.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: 'Bulky item delivery', 'Staircase fee (S$10 per floor)' and 'Disposal fee' are explained inline, but 'Platform fee' leans on an info icon.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: It asks only for address, deal method, payment and an optional promo code, all things the buyer knows at checkout.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Add-on fee details sit as small sub-lines under 'Delivery add-on' and the platform fee hides behind its info icon.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Every section is checkout content for this buyer; the seller phone is a separate actor, not part of this screen.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Section titles and values ('PayNow', 'S$550.00') carry it; only the one-line terms note above 'Place order' is prose.
